IS 1 7705- 1975 

Indian Standard 

m 

CODE OF PRACTICE FOR 

PACKAGING OF PRECISION AND SPECIAL 

PURPOSE STEEL TUBES 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 27 June 1975, after the draft finalized by the Engineering Goods 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement 
and Packaging Division Council. 

0.2 It has been observed that precision and special purpose steel tubes 
used for automobiles, bicycles, transformers, boilers, heat exchangers and 
furniture, are usually damaged in transit, when not properly packed* 
This standard was prepared with the feeling that a code of practice for 
packaging of precision steel tubes will help the packaging of such tubes. 

J3 The recommended practices for packaging of steel tubes for general 
purposes are covered in IS : 4740-1968*. 

eeieeMamavneemvemmmnamnmememmn^ammmnai 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard lays down recommended practice for packaging of 
precision and special purpose steel tubes. 

2. PROTECTION AGAINST RUST 

» 

2.1 All tubes shall be treated inside and outside with rust preventive oils 
conforming to IS : 958-1958f, IS : 1 153-1957$, IS : 1 154-1957§, or IS : 1674- 
1960||. 

2*2 Tubes that are galvanised may not be dipped in ofl. 

2*3 The manufacturers may select suitable rust preventive depending on 
the distance, time and the mode of transportation involved. Any different 
specification indicated by the customer shall be agreed to between the 
manufacturer and the customer. 



♦Code of practice for packaging of steel tabes* 

fSpecifieation for temporary corrosion preventive crease, toft film, cold application. 
^Specification for temporary corrosion preventive fluid, bard film, advent deposited, 
specification for temporary corrosion preventive fluid, soft film, solvent deposited, 
water displacing* 

IBpesfieation fbr temporary corrosion preventive fluid, soft film, solvent deposited. 



IS 1 7705. 1975 

3. METHOD OF PACKING 

3.1 Fall Length Tabes — Any one of the following methods may be 
used for packaging of full length tubes as agreed to between the manu- 
facturer and the purchaser. 

3.1.1 Suitable number of tubes shall be made into a bundle and tied 
together at 3 to 6 places with annealed steel wire of 2 to 3*2 mm diameter 
or poly-propylcnc or coir rope of appropriate strength equally spaced. 

3.1.2 The bundles of tubes of length not exceeding 7 m shall have their 
ends covered with hessian or bitumanized hessian, bound securely with 
annealed steel wire of 2 to 3*2 mm diameter or poly-propylcnc or cotr rope 
of appropriate strength at a distance of 20 to 30 cm from either end. 
There may be one or two more bindings on the bundles equally spaced 
from the ends. 

3.1.2.1 For export purposes the bands on either side of the centre 
shall have an additional loop to facilitate slinging. 

3.1.3 Necessary handling hoops shall be provided for handling the 
bundles with forklift trucks, gantries, etc. The lifting zones are to be 
marked on the bundles. Spacers are to be provided for long pipes. 
Grates shall have slingrebts or fork rest pieces so that pipes are not 
damaged due to handling. 

3.2 Got Length Tubes — Cut length tubes shall be packed in wooden 
boxes or crates. The boxes or crates shall be lined inside with waterproof 
paper or bituminized hessian cloth or bituminized polythene faced hessian 
cloth. The boxes after filling shall be closed by nailing and fastened with 
mild steel strap 40 X 0*71 mm or 20 to 25 X 0*45 to 0*55 mm. The weight 
of the wooden crates shall not exceed 400 kg. 

Norn— The bandies as specified in 3.1.1 and 34J2 but not intended for export 
tbonld not weigh more than 100 kg which it normally considered conrenient for the 
purpose of handling, loading and unloading operations. The number of tubes per 
bundle shall be determined by the diameter and gauge of the tubes. 

4. MARKING 

4*1 The following information shall be marked on the wooden crate or on 
a metal tag tied to the bundle: 

a) Paiticulanofthe tube — site, gauge and length; 

b) Any information required by the purchaser; and 

c) Handling instructiona, if any. hi accordance with 
IS: 1260 ( Part H)-1973«.
